name: Decagon
title: A forecast that can explain every movement
subtitle: RevOps · Analytics engineering · GTM leadership
focus: Turn CRM history into tested, documented models that make pipeline, conversion and forecast movement understandable.
priorities: Build the foundational GTM analytics models.
Join Salesforce, Gong and Outreach context in BigQuery.
Develop tested transformations and repeatable reporting with dbt and Hex.
Partner with RevOps and leadership on trusted definitions and self-service.
layers: Immutable opportunity and activity snapshots with source and event time.
Account, opportunity, stage history and activity grains documented separately.
Unique opportunity keys, valid stage transitions and reconciled amount definitions.
Pipeline movement, cohorts and self-service views with a clear owner for each metric.
rules: A current opportunity row cannot reconstruct the full stage history.
Reopened and pushed opportunities need an explicit movement category.
Separate weighted forecast assumptions from committed forecast and actual revenue.

personas.name: RevOps leader
personas.pain: Conflicting metrics and opaque stage movement
personas.promise: Tested models with a clear grain, definition and reporting as-of time.
personas.subject: The bridge behind {{forecast_period}}
personas.email: Hi {{first_name}}, I’d start with one question: can the team explain the movement from last week’s pipeline to this week’s? A small bridge of new, advanced, pushed and resized opportunities is a useful place to agree on definitions. Which movement is hardest to reconcile today?
personas.question: Which metric has two competing definitions, and who owns the resolution?

personas.name: CX transformation leader
personas.pain: An evaluation with several stakeholders and unclear success criteria
personas.promise: A coordinated evaluation plan with an explicit baseline and decision owner.
personas.subject: A clear evaluation for {{support_workflow}}
personas.email: Hi {{first_name}}, a support-agent evaluation is easier to judge when the team agrees on the workflow, baseline and escalation path first. Which support journey would be useful to evaluate, and what would your team need to see to make a decision?
personas.question: Who owns the evaluation baseline, security review and final decision?

pitch: I bring commercial context to data-system work. I have managed complex technical sales, built a source-backed extraction pipeline and built a local CRM with deduplicated imports and pipeline stages. At Decagon, I would focus that experience on explicit definitions, reliable history and analytics that help RevOps and leadership explain what changed and what to do next.
mappings: Hey Sammy: validation, deduplication, structured records and bounded recovery.
Define opportunity and activity grains before joining them.
Local CRM pipeline stages and PostHog funnel work.
Build a repeatable pipeline movement view with clear definitions.
Enterprise technical sales through validation, proposals and negotiation.
Translate the questions leaders and sellers ask into useful model outputs.
weekOne: One reconciled pipeline movement view with RevOps-owned definitions.
days60: Extend tested models to stage conversion and activity context, then publish a documented self-service reporting view.
days90: Make forecast and cohort reviews repeatable; prioritize the next models from the questions business teams still cannot answer.

firstBuilds.title: Pipeline movement model
firstBuilds.goal: Make changes explainable before building more reporting.
firstBuilds.scope: A bounded period and one leadership metric reviewed with RevOps.
firstBuilds.measure: Reconciliation variance, unclassified changes and time to answer a business question.

firstBuilds.title: Opportunity history foundation
firstBuilds.goal: Keep stage changes and timing available for repeatable cohort analysis.
firstBuilds.scope: One stage-history source and a small representative account cohort.
firstBuilds.measure: Missing timestamps, duplicate keys and source-to-model freshness.

firstBuilds.title: Self-service GTM reporting
firstBuilds.goal: Help the commercial team answer common questions with shared definitions.
firstBuilds.scope: One RevOps partner and three repeated leadership questions.
firstBuilds.measure: Answer accuracy, repeat usage and avoided ad hoc reconstruction.
